heading: CHAPTER I

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Region of East Barito Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government Administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of East Barito.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives Institution which is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus of East Barito Regency is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regional House of Representatives of East Barito Regency in the administration of government affairs which are the authority of East Barito Regency.

Office is a Regional Apparatus that manages government affairs in the field of women and children.

Technical Service Unit is a Regional Technical Service Unit that manages the affairs of protection of women and children.

Child is a person who is not yet 18 years old, including a child who is still in the womb.

Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a Woman.

Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.

Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.

Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.

Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and/or causes death.

Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

16. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
17. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
1g. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.

19. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.

20. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance.
21. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to the family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of their needs.
22. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
24. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
25. Regional Action Plan hereinafter abbreviated as RAD is a foundation and guideline for related offices, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

26. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to provide protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
27. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
28. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and sideways up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.

Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the annual financial plan of the Regional Government which is discussed and approved jointly by the Regional Government and DPRD and stipulated by Regional Regulation.

Gender Equality is the view that all people should receive equal treatment and not be discriminated against based on their gender identity.

Medicolegal Service is a form of health service carried out by medical personnel using medical science and technology based on the authority possessed for legal purposes and to implement applicable regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XII
CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

SANCTION PROVISIONS

Article 24

(1) Any person who intentionally does not provide protection for women and children resulting in acts of violence, allows acts of violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the Laws and Regulations.

(2) If officials appointed to provide protection do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities, they shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

3. Officials who carry out service and protection duties for Children and Women from acts of violence, who violate service principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the internal organizational mechanism.

heading: CHAPTER XIV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIV

OTHER PROVISIONS

Article 25

The handling of legal cases in the investigation process (1) by law enforcement officers must be handled by special investigators who have been appointed according to their competence by law enforcement institutions for the field of protection of women and children.

Special investigators as referred to in paragraph (2) (1) are:

a. in cases of investigation for women or female children victims of violence must be handled by female investigators;

b. the implementation process as referred to in letter a must be in a closed room attended only by the victim's parents or guardian along with the advocacy and psychology team from P3A who have the same gender;

c. investigations for male children victims of violence may be conducted by male or female investigators, preferably of the same gender and carried out as referred to in letter b; and

d. The trial process is not open to the public.

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

In the case of trial proceedings related to cases of violence against children, the presence of the child does not necessarily have to be presented at the trial, except in circumstances that are very compelling while still separating the meeting between the child and the perpetrator in trial processes at different times.

heading: Article 27
Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

The news media is not permitted to expose news coverage for cases concerning child victims of sexual violence in order to protect the child's identity and their hope for future life except if the victim loses their life as a result of such violence.

heading: CHAPTER XIT
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIT

FUNDING

Article 29

The budget allocation for protection of women and children victims of violence carried out by the Regional Government is sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, and/or other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XVI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XVI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 30

The establishment of UPT as referred to in Article 9 paragraph (3) must be implemented no later than 1 (one) year from the enactment of this Regional Regulation.

translated_text:
Article 31

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, it is ordered that this Regional Regulation be promulgated by placing it in the Regional Gazette of East Barito Regency.

heading: CONCERNING
translated_text:
CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

The role of women is very important because they are the mothers of the nation who are the pillars of the family to build the future of quality human resources in various fields including family economic empowerment, likewise with children who are the nation's generation who will play a role in filling development in the future.

Children and Women must receive protection from violence, exploitation, human trafficking and neglect by responsible parties. Protection is intended to create a peaceful and prosperous atmosphere for all levels of society in fostering life and togetherness within the regional area. Violence cannot be avoided just like that, but must be prevented as early as possible from spreading to a level that is detrimental to all parties. Protection efforts are prioritized on prevention efforts and minimizing incidents.

Acts of violence against Children and Women are violations of human rights so their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life is guaranteed in accordance with their nature and destiny without discrimination. So far, laws and regulations governing the protection of Children and Women victims of violence have not regulated protection efforts in the Region so institutional and regulatory support is needed that can guarantee their implementation. Regional Regulations regulate protection efforts for victims, especially in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of Children and Women victims of violence in Kotabaru Regency. As one of the efforts to protect Children and Women, it is carried out through guidance, training and assistance to victims and families of violence victims. Economic empowerment is also carried out for the prevention of women as victims, which can be done by growing and developing micro and small businesses in accordance with local potential. To grow micro and small businesses, it is necessary to increase the capacity and capability of women through assistance and guidance so that women can develop their businesses.

heading: Article 2
translated_text:
Article 2

Paragraph (1) Letter a Respect for the rights of Children and Women is respect for the fulfillment of basic rights for women and children.

Letter b What is meant by "gender justice and equality" is a condition where every person, both men and women, is treated equally and obtains equal opportunities to gain access, as well as welfare; Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of the victim" is all the best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter e What is meant by restoration of socio-economic rights is increasing understanding, awareness, responsibility, commitment, participation, ability and independence in order to improve the economy and quality of women or target groups so as to avoid problems.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.

heading: Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

Paragraph (1) "physical violence" means any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death. "psychological violence" means an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. "sexual violence" means any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. "exploitation" includes:

a. acts that exploit a child economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;

the act with or without the victim's consent that

b. includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

"trafficking in persons" means the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.

"Household Neglect" means:

a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social;

b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of a child as appropriate;

c. acts that neglect a person within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person;

d. acts that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

What is meant by deviant behavior of children is such as the use of glue that can cause children to feel addicted or intoxicated because they are invited by their friends, and deviations towards promiscuous sexual behavior or the use of illicit goods.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear.
